# Compacted Summary: Chapter 1 (Complete and Final – Updated 34)

## Setting and Time
- **Season/Period**: Spring through late August, then Christmas/New Year period of first year; now nearly three weeks into new year (1832)
- **Primary Location**: Middlemarch and surrounding areas (Lowick, the Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Wilhaven, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Salmere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Salwick)
- **Atmospheric Details**: Baker's boy frequently late; wind off water with salt and tar smell; dog barking periodically; bees in lavender behind parsonage; gulls quarreling over fish heads; carts with turnips; frost silvering hedges; road rutted and puddled after thaw; children chasing hoops down lane; bell for vespers ringing thinly; chalk sun on forge wall; smoke from chimneys lying flat over fields; rain threatening but holding off
- **Secondary Characters/Background**: Ilrine Corrett (herbalist), Eldette Corrett (cooper), Thidrek Corrett (smith), Ridan Corrett (glazier), Jotho Corrett; Aessa Hollwood (ferryman), Cotho Hollwood (mason), Halan Hollwood (shepherd), Ulvie Hollwood (weaver), Thiena Hollwood (glazier); Elnar Brackwood (weaver), Senelle Brackwood (ferryman), Jovus Brackwood (miller), Madan Brackwood (scribe), Cotho Brackwood (shepherd), Tassa Brackwood (weaver); Colan Lindson (born at Quenwick), Islis Lindson (shepherd, born at Quenwick), Movie Lindson (weaver), Maric Lindson (mason, born at Quenwick, called "Old Maric"); Ridette Lindson (tanner); Orrine Stenworth (mason); Feena Stenworth (miller); Rira Stenworth (cooper, born at Wilhaven); Nynelle Stenworth (ferryman); Ilzek Wexwood (smith, born in Staveton); Daena Wexwood (mason, born in Salwick); Mrs. Abel (housekeeper at Stone Court), Mr. Abel; Mrs. Dollop (spirited landlady of Tankard in Slaughter Lane); Mr. Dill (barber); Fletcher (Hawley's clerk, has bad finger)

## Main Characters

**Dorothea**
- Recently widowed; residing at Lowick Manor
- Strong admiration for Caleb Garth's work knowledge; hopes to improve land and build good cottages
- Final Grange encounter: Will declared best is over, would live like one who saw heaven in trance
- Mistakenly believed Will's words referred to Mrs. Lydgate; experienced certainty his conduct with Rosamond should be above suspicion
- Though thought she might be what Will cared for most, doubt overcame this; credited all to friendship and obstruction from Casaubon's codicil
- Saw Will with portfolio on road; felt pang leaving him behind
- Forced to keep money under Casaubon's codicil that ought to have been Will's
- **Bulstrode's Report**: Described as "a woman of most munificent disposition" in possession of funds she can well spare; destined chief part of funds to another purpose; willing to consider taking Bulstrode's place in relation to Hospital; setting out on journey into Yorkshire with Sir James and Lady Chettam; her decision regarding Hospital contribution will depend on conclusions about land she is to see there

**Will Ladislaw**
- Passionate love for Dorothea which he forbade himself to utter; silence maintained because she was forced to keep money that ought to have been his
- After parting: certainty had much more bitterness; had no assurance she loved him
- Still at Middlemarch despite weeks since parting; frequenting Lydgate's household; warbling continually with Rosamond (scandal spreading per Mrs. Cadwallader)
- Raffles knows connection between Will and Bulstrode but deliberately conceals this as card to play
- Father was at Boulogne very ill; mother's family engaged in "respectable thieving line"; mother (Sarah) ran away after Archie Duncan rejected her
- Rejected Bulstrode's money; stated unblemished honor and unstained birth important; recognized stain through mother; refuses "ill-gotten money"
- Wrote brief letter to Dorothea asking permission to call at Lowick
- **Public Scandal**: His genealogy now public knowledge in Middlemarch via Bambridge's disclosure at Green Dragon; described as having "queer genealogy"—high-spirited young lady (Dorothea's aunt), musical Polish patriot, with "grafting of the Jew pawnbroker" (Bulstrode's pawnbroker business connection); scandal raises questions about his legitimacy and inheritance rights

**Caleb Garth**
- Working with railroads: measured and valued outlying piece of land at Yoddrell's farm belonging to Lowick Manor
- Decided to take Fred Vincy on as assistant with desk-work and accounts; offered eighty pounds for first year, more after
- **Stone Court Opportunity**: Consulted by Bulstrode on farm management; advised against mere bailiff; alluring idea occurred to Caleb—what if Fred Vincy could be placed at Stone Court under Caleb's management responsibility?
- **Critical Moral Moment with Raffles**: Took up Raffles in his gig after Raffles got down from coach; Raffles recognized Caleb from previous meeting at Stone Court with Bulstrode; Caleb saw Raffles was ill and provided shelter
- **Final Confrontation with Bulstrode—Moral Firmness**: When Bulstrode attempted to continue business arrangement, Caleb made firm declaration: must request Bulstrode put business into other hands; must give it up because obliged to believe Raffles has told him truth about Bulstrode's harmful past life (Bulstrode led harmful life for gain, kept others out of their rights by deceit); can't be happy working with Bulstrode; promised not to pass on what Raffles told him unless something unknown forces it from him; acknowledged if Bulstrode repents for keeping others out of their rights by deceit, he must want to go back but can't; has not judged him as wicked or righteous; a man may do wrong and his will may rise clear out of it, though he can't get his life clear; that's bad punishment
- Now raising his hat with mild gravity when encountering Bulstrode

**Mary Garth**
- Staying at Lowick Rectory with Miss Farebrother and Mrs. Farebrother
- Told Farebrother: "I have too strong a feeling for Fred to give him up for any one else"
- Upon Fred telling her of engagement with her father, touched keenly; scolded him for not seeing Farebrother's delicate feeling
- Earnestly desired to be clear she loved Fred best; determined to watch over her affections and constancy
- Currently telling Rumpelstiltskin tale to children at Lowick Parsonage; Fred seated near her, watching with admiration

**Fred Vincy**
- Age four-and-twenty; son of Mr. Vincy; rejected Church vocation; took degree
- Encountered Caleb Garth at Yoddrell's farm; accepted eighty pounds for first year, more after
- Mr. Vincy responded with profound surprise and cutting disappointment; will keep no horse for Fred
- Casually mentioned to Rosamond what he heard about Casaubon's codicil mentioning Ladislaw
- Billiard room incident: encountered Lydgate gambling; felt shock; old opinion of Lydgate as prig reversed
- **Farebrother's Intervention and Warning**: Farebrother drew Fred aside at St. Botolph's; confessed temptation to let Fred go wrong; disclosed satisfaction of Fred's affections stands in way of his own; warned Mary's affection is "conditionally bound" and liable to change; Fred seized by uncomfortable chill; Farebrother overcame temptation and uttered warning instead of selfish action
- At Lowick Parsonage: seated near Mary during storytelling; watching her with admiration

**Mr. Lydgate**
- Doctor/physician; age nine-and-twenty
- **Financial Crisis Resolved**: Debt amounted to three hundred and eighty pounds at Brassing; creditor Mr. Dover held bill of sale on furniture; Dover's agent was put in house; Bulstrode offered thousand pounds to free him from burdens; Lydgate accepted this offer; received cash to pay Dover's agent
- **Emotional Conflict About the Loan**: As he canted home with good news for Rosamond, thought crossed his mind with unpleasant impression—contrast in himself which few months had brought; he should be overjoyed at being under strong personal obligation but was uneasy; relation of personal indebtedness to Bulstrode was what he had once been most resolved to avoid; worried Bulstrode's motives for sudden beneficence might be merely selfish
- **Arrived at Stone Court Morning of Raffles's Death**: Arrived at half-past ten in time to witness final pause of breath; when entering room, sudden expression in Lydgate's face showed recognition that he had not judged correctly; stood by bed in silence, eyes turned on dying man, with subdued activity of expression showing inward debate
- **Uneasy About Case**: Was in state of recovered hope and freedom; had set out on work with all old animation; felt himself strong enough to bear all deficiencies of married life; conscious that Bulstrode had been a benefactor to him; but was uneasy about this case; had not expected it to terminate as it had done; hardly knew how to put question to Bulstrode without appearing to insult him
- **Return to Middlemarch with Bulstrode**: He and Bulstrode rode back together, talking of many things—chiefly cholera and chances of the Reform Bill in the House of Lords, and firm resolve of political Unions; nothing was said about Raffles except that Bulstrode mentioned necessity of having grave for him in Lowick churchyard
- **Conversation with Farebrother**: Told Farebrother he can enjoy kindness all the more because he is happier, having been good deal crushed; acknowledged fear bruises will be painful later but torture-screw is off; disclosed plans to set up surgery and take apprentice, saying "if Rosamond will not mind"; acknowledged severe galling to begin with
- **Treatment Philosophy**: Strongly convinced against prevalent practice of allowing alcohol and administering large doses of opium in alcoholic poisoning cases; repeatedly acted on this conviction with favorable result
- **Medical Care of Raffles**: Gave chief instruction to Bulstrode on administration of extremely moderate doses of opium in case of sleeplessness continuing; brought opium in pocket; gave minute directions as to doses and point at which they should cease; insisted on risk of not ceasing; repeated order that no alcohol should be given
- **Public Scandal and Suspicion**: Now subject of public scandal spread by Mrs. Dollop and others at Tankard; accused of being willing to cut up everybody before breath was well out of their body; rumored to use invisible drugs to kill; townspeople speculating about his complicity in Raffles's death; does not yet know distinctly why people are looking strangely at him
- **Town Hall Meeting**: Present at sanitary meeting held in Town-Hall on cholera burial-ground question; arrived with Bulstrode; entered together and took seats near head of large central table
- **After Public Exposure of Bulstrode**: When Bulstrode was confronted at Town Hall meeting with public accusations, Lydgate underwent shock as from terrible practical interpretation of some faint augury; felt resentful hatred checked by healer's instinct to bring rescue or relief; looked at Bulstrode's shrunken misery; after Bulstrode was asked to leave by Mr. Thesiger, rose and gave his arm to trembling Bulstrode to lead him out; felt this act of compassion was unspeakably bitter to him; realized it appeared to others as putting his sign-manual to association with Bulstrode; now feels full conviction that Bulstrode gave him thousand pounds as bribe and that treatment of Raffles had been tampered with from evil motive; understands town knows of loan, believes it bribe, and believes he took it as bribe

**Rosamond Lydgate (née Vincy)**
- Married to Lydgate; victorious obstinacy never wasting energy
- **Manipulation and Consequences**: Manipulated husband to go riding; accident at Halsell Wood led to loss of baby; regaining brilliant health
- Possesses knowledge of Casaubon's codicil mentioning Will
- **Response to Debt Crisis**: When Lydgate proposed debt must be paid, fell like mortal chill; when presented with house-selling proposal, went to Mrs. Plymdale with congratulations instead; had secretly disobeyed by asking father for help; father said more likely to want help himself; called on Mr. Borthrop Trumbull at his office; revoked Lydgate's order before New Year's Day party
- **Written to Sir Godwin with Refusal**: Had written requesting aid; awaited answer for nearly three weeks; Sir Godwin refused all aid; stated wife should not write on business
- **Current Status**: Likely gone to stay with her parents while crisis continues

**Mr. Bulstrode**
- **Raffles's Care and Death**: After initial investigation of Raffles's pockets at Stone Court, found bills showing stay at inn at Bilkley (forty miles from Middlemarch); Lydgate gave specific treatment instructions with moderate opium doses and strict prohibition on alcohol
- **Evening of Care**: At six o'clock when Raffles still wakeful and restless, Bulstrode began administering opium according to Lydgate's directions; after half hour called Mrs. Abel and told her he found himself unfit for further watching; repeated Lydgate's directions to her; Mrs. Abel had not before known anything of Lydgate's prescriptions
- **Raffles's Death and Relief**: Raffles died during night; by morning, Bulstrode felt more at rest than he had done for many months; his conscience was soothed by enfolding wing of secrecy
- **Public Exposure of Past**: At Green Dragon, discovered his past publicly betrayed by Bambridge at the inn; Bambridge heard information from party who was old chum of Bulstrode's (likely Raffles), picked up at Bilkley; story concerns Bulstrode's rise to fortune and involvement with pawnbroker's business; now widespread public scandal and conjecture about his past life; townspeople (including Mrs. Dollop at Tankard, Mr. Baldwin) openly discussing his crimes; described as having brought money to town by thieving and swindling; spreading theory he killed Raffles
- **Social Consequences**: Townspeople turning against him; pressure mounting; his standing as Bank manager and Hospital benefactor affected
- **Plans for Change and Current Status**: Change of plan determined by severe experience since Raffles recognized Will Ladislaw; contemplates temporary withdrawal from management of much business; thinking of changing residence for a time; probably will close or let 'The Shrubs' and take place near coast under advice as to salubrity
- **Made Up Mind About Middlemarch**: Taking journeys on business of various kinds; has now made up his mind that he need not quit Middlemarch; feeling able consequently to determine on matters which he had before left in suspense
- **Anxiety About Hospital**: Avoids saying anything further to Lydgate about Hospital, fearing to manifest too sudden change of plans immediately on death of Raffles; in his secret soul believes that Lydgate suspects his orders to have been intentionally disobeyed, and suspecting this must also suspect a motive
- **Town Hall Meeting—Public Confrontation**: Present at sanitary meeting; started from Bank before noon with intention of urging plan of private subscription; felt he should resume his old position as man of action and influence in public affairs of the town; joined Lydgate and entered meeting together
- **Exposure and Collapse**: When Mr. Hawley publicly denounced him with accusations of virulent hatred and malpractices, Bulstrode went through crisis of feeling almost too violent for his delicate frame to support; experienced quick vision that his life was failure, that he was dishonored man, must quail before glance of those toward whom he had habitually assumed attitude of reprover; sensed God had disowned him before men; felt utter futility in equivocation with his conscience in dealing with life of his accomplice, an equivocation which now turned venomously upon him with full-grown fang of discovered lie; all this rushed through him like agony of terror which fails to kill; sudden sense of exposure after re-established sense of safety came not to coarse organization of criminal, but to susceptible nerve of man whose intensest being lay in such mastery and predominance as conditions of his life had shaped
- **Response and Attempted Defense**: Through bodily infirmity ran tenacious nerve of ambitious self-preserving will, continually leaping out like flame, scattering all doctrinal fears; beginning to stir and glow under ashy paleness; before last words were out of Hawley's mouth, felt he should answer with a retort; dared not stand and declare innocence; sat perfectly still leaning hard against back of chair; when began to speak pressed hands upon seat; voice hoarser than usual, words distinctly pronounced though paused between sentences short of breath; protested as Christian minister against sanction of proceedings dictated by virulent hatred; pointed out hostile men glad to believe any libel; voice rose and took on biting accent when addressed accusations of malpractices; called upon accusers to inspect his professional life; repudiated Hawley's "canting palavering Christianity"; stated does not maintain thieves and cheat offspring of their due inheritance to support religion; called upon accusers to enter into satisfactory explanations or withdraw from posts; stated they decline to co-operate with man whose character not cleared from infamous lights
- **Forced Departure**: After Thesiger recommended he quit room to avoid further hindrance to business, Bulstrode took hat from floor and slowly rose after moment's hesitation; grasped corner of chair so totteringly that Lydgate felt sure he had not strength to walk away without support; Lydgate rose and gave him his arm, leading him out of room

**Mr. Farebrother (Vicar)**
- **Intervention with Fred and Mary**: Left whist-table to speak with Lydgate, disclosing Lydgate had done him service by influencing him to stop playing for money; later approached Fred at billiard-table; confessed temptation to let Fred ruin himself; disclosed satisfaction of Fred's affections stands in way of his own; warned Mary's affection is "conditionally bound"; claimed another man might win firm place through companionship of ready sympathy; overcame temptation to act selfishly
- **Response to Lydgate's Beneficence**: When Lydgate mentioned Bulstrode's financial aid, Farebrother compelled himself to approve of man whom he disliked; said Bulstrode must naturally feel interest in Lydgate's welfare after working with him in way reducing his income
- **After Town Hall Meeting**: Walking back to Lowick with Mr. Brooke; deeply mournful regarding Lydgate's situation; with keen perception of human weakness, could not be confident that under pressure of humiliating needs Lydgate had not fallen below himself
- Seated opposite Mr. Hawley at Town Hall meeting; watching Mary Garth with evident admiration

**Mr. Brooke**
- Before Bulstrode's public exposure at Town Hall, had heard only imperfect hints and felt uneasy he had "gone a little too far" in countenancing Bulstrode
- Now got himself fully informed and felt benevolent sadness talking to Farebrother about ugly light in which Lydgate had come to be regarded
- Drove along with Farebrother heading toward Lowick; chatting with good-natured hope there had not really been anything black in Lydgate's behavior; described Lydgate as young fellow quite above common mark when brought letter from uncle Sir Godwin

**Mr. Raffles**
- **DECEASED**: Died during night at Stone Court following Bulstrode's administration of opium
- Known to Bulstrode from twenty-five years prior; addressed him as "Nick"
- Revealed to Caleb Garth information about Bulstrode's harmful past life
- **Disclosure of Secrets**: Before death, disclosed Bulstrode's pawnbroker past and financial maneuverings to Bambridge at Bilkley; this information now public in Middlemarch; Bambridge spread story at Green Dragon and throughout town

## Public Scandal and Town Opinion
- Mrs. Dollop at Tankard leading public discourse; describing Bulstrode as suspicious character; openly theorizing Lydgate poisoned Raffles with invisible drugs; conjecture about Raffles being "ticed to a lone house" and dying under suspicious circumstances
- Mrs. Dollop notes Lydgate recently paid off Mr. Byles the butcher for bill running since last Michaelmas, suggesting he received sudden funds
- **Theory Solidified**: Bulstrode paid for Raffles's death through Lydgate; town knows of loan, believes it bribe, believes Lydgate took it as bribe
- **Public Confrontation at Town Hall**: Hawley publicly denounced Bulstrode with accusations of thieving, swindling, and malpractices; demanded he clear himself or withdraw from posts; stated they decline to co-operate with him
- Consensus: Something nefarious occurred; scandal affecting both Bulstrode's and Lydgate's reputations despite latter's medical innocence
